spec.title: Widen the two Lane-1 phase derivations to the writer, and DECLARE 0-setup
spec.problem: `commands/pipeline.md` writes 28 `current_phase` ASSIGNMENT OCCURRENCES (grain: occurrences). Those resolve to 27 DISTINCT literal strings, of which 26 are CONCRETE and the 27th is the `<phase>-error` TEMPLATE (grain: distinct strings). Two Lane-1 test suites (tests/test-voice-lint.sh and tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh) derive only 27 occurrences / 26 distinct / 25 concrete, because their pattern requires an unquoted key (`current_phase: "..."`) while pipeline.md:53 writes one assignment in JSON form (`"current_phase": "0-setup"`) inside the Phase 0 block. The literal missing at every one of those grains is the same single literal, `0-setup`. Both suites then assert that every phase they FOUND is accounted for in the tables they police, and both pass. `0-setup` is accounted for nowhere: it is in neither voice-lint.mjs's VOICE_MOMENTS nor its NON_VOICE_PHASES, and in none of gate-phase-entry.mjs's PREREQUISITES / UNGUARDED / TERMINAL. The anti-vacuity control cannot see this, because the assertion and its control range over the same narrowed set: a phase the pattern cannot see is not an unaccounted phase, it is not a phase at all. Verified at HEAD c04b47c: both suites are green (48/0 and 37/0) with the defect live, and the voice-lint control prints the wrong population as a reassurance (`found 26`). The consequence at runtime is silence in both directions. A record at `0-setup` gets no voice check (the documented fail-open path; measured: exit 0, zero bytes of output, where the identical message at `5-archived` exits 2 with five named failures). And the phase-entry guard's decision reason for `0-setup` carries a JUDGEMENT CLAUSE byte-identical to the one it produces for an invented phase `9-invented` -- 31 bytes, `, which is not a guarded phase.` -- so the run's first phase is currently judged as if it were a typo. (The full reason strings differ, because the guard interpolates the record's own phase into the prefix; the identity is in the clause, not the string, and that distinction is what makes this criterion falsifiable at all -- see AC7.)
spec.root_cause: Two independent things, and they must be fixed together or the fix is cosmetic. (1) THE DERIVATION is narrower than its subject: the pattern encodes ONE of the two quoting forms pipeline.md uses, and the only control over it is a count floor computed from the same pattern. (2) THE DECISION was made and recorded backwards: test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh rules against the loose form BY NAME in a comment (re-derive with `git grep -n 'so the two checks would disagree'`) saying it 'picks up 0-setup from the Phase 0 JSON block, so the two checks would disagree about their own population.' The comment is right that they disagree and wrong about which one is right. The narrower choice made the two Lane-1 suites agree with each other and disagree with the writer, and with the third derivation in tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh (re-derive with `git grep -n 'PIPELINE_PHASES=' -- plugins/pipeline/tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh`) which has been on the loose form since #34/#42. NOTE ON THE FIX'S OWN SHAPE, added in rework round 1: replacing one pattern with a wider pattern does not close the class -- it moves the boundary. The class closes only when the coverage control's POPULATION is something no assignment spelling can escape (the bare word `current_phase`), with every occurrence forced into a named bucket.
requirements: R1. Both Lane-1 derivations (tests/test-voice-lint.sh and tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh) must claim EVERY current_phase assignment pipeline.md writes, in every quoting form the writer uses, so each suite's population equals its subject. At HEAD that is 26 concrete literals (27 distinct minus the `<phase>-error` template), up from 25. Any exact-count pin over that population (drift suite `literalCount == 25`) is replaced by, or accompanied by, an assertion over the LABEL SET, so a future literal cannot be absorbed by editing one number (#33). SWEEP, so the fold-in is checkable rather than asserted: Lane 1 holds FIVE copies of the strict pattern and this change accounts for all five -- test-voice-lint.sh's derivation AND its separate count line, the drift suite's main derivation, the drift suite's Checkpoint-first `sed` extraction (AC8), and the drift suite's `-complete` sub-derivation (AC9). Re-derive the list with `git grep -n 'current_phase: \*"' -- plugins/pipeline/tests`, which returns exactly those five at HEAD. A SIXTH strict-form site, test-gate-phase-entry.sh's md61() helper, is SAFE today because both its live terms name phases written in unquoted-key form; it takes a comment stating the limit, not a rewrite. DBA confirmed the Checkpoint-first copy and the `-complete` copy in Phase 2 round 2; both are covered here, and neither is left as the fourth or fifth copy of a pattern this issue exists to widen.

R2. Each Lane-1 suite carries a FORM-COVERAGE control whose POPULATION IS EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE SUBJECT, not a third guess at assignment syntax. The property: every occurrence of the BARE WORD `current_phase` in pipeline.md lands in exactly one of three buckets -- CLAIMED by that suite's derivation, EXCLUDED by a rule the suite STATES, or UNCLASSIFIED -- UNCLASSIFIED is empty, and the EXCLUDED bucket is EXHIBITED BY NAME on every run with its MEMBERSHIP asserted and its size only reported. The bare word is the right population precisely because no assignment spelling can leave it: single-quoted value, backtick value, key/value split across a newline, unquoted YAML value, `.current_phase = "x"`, a wide gap before the colon -- each lands visibly in a bucket instead of being deleted by a pre-filter. CORRECTION TO ROUND 0: the previous wording pinned the population to a permissive REGEX ANCHOR and claimed that generalised 'to a quoting form nobody has invented yet'. That claim was FALSE as written and is withdrawn. Measured on a fixture carrying seven assignment forms plus one prose mention: the anchor version finds 1 of 8 bare-word occurrences and reports UNCLAIMED = 0, GREEN, while six real assignments are invisible to both the assertion and its control -- byte-for-byte the shape of the #53 defect, one level up, inside #53's own fix. The tri-partition version reports 6 UNCLASSIFIED BY NAME on the same fixture. HONEST RESIDUAL, RESTATED IN ROUND 2 because round 1's answer was aimed at the safe direction: the EXCLUSION RULE is itself a spelling and can swallow a real assignment, and PINNING THE EXCLUDED BUCKET'S SIZE DOES NOT CATCH THAT -- a swallowed assignment paired with a deleted prose mention holds every bucket size constant (measured, see AC2/AC3). Two things close it instead, and both are required. FIRST, the exclusion rule is not an independently spelled third rule but the NEGATION OF A PATTERN STRICTLY WIDER THAN THE CLAIM PATTERN, so the claim rule and the exclusion rule cannot disagree about what an assignment operator is -- which is the disagreement SecOps demonstrated (`current_phase = "0-setup"` is claimed by neither and excluded by round 1's stated rule, so it lands in EXCLUDED silently). SECOND, the EXCLUDED bucket's MEMBERSHIP is asserted, not its cardinality: the size pin is withdrawn as a #33 violation, raised independently by both Phase 2 reviewers, and the sorted membership list subsumes the size anyway.

R3. `0-setup` is DECLARED in voice-lint.mjs as a non-voice phase, with the MECHANISM that makes it non-voice recorded beside it and the GENERAL condition under which that stops being true. Mechanism: pipeline.md's Phase 0 step 1 (the dirty-worktree halt, the one owner-facing full-voice decision block in Phase 0) runs BEFORE step 5 writes status.json, so a turn can never end at `0-setup` in that halt. EXPIRY, stated generally rather than as the single reversal: the declaration is wrong the moment ANY full-voice owner-facing decision block comes to sit between the step that writes `current_phase: "0-setup"` and the next Checkpoint-first write. That is a strictly wider and likelier condition than 'if steps 1 and 5 reverse', and it is checkable: measured at HEAD, pipeline.md has exactly one full-voice decision block in Phase 0 (line 44, step 1), the `0-setup` write is at line 53, the next Checkpoint-first site is at line 131, and there are ZERO full-voice/decision-block mentions between 53 and 131.

R4. `0-setup` is DECLARED in gate-phase-entry.mjs's partition, in a cell whose stated semantics are true of it. A PREREQUISITES row is REFUSED BY NAME: ENTRY is derived from PREREQUISITES keys and must equal the SET of phases pipeline.md names at Checkpoint-first sites (see AC8), `0-setup` is not written at a Checkpoint-first site, and that invariant is correct and load-bearing. Widening UNGUARDED or adding a fifth partition cell are both legal; the RECOMMENDATION is now the fifth cell on COMPATIBILITY grounds, not stylistic ones -- see open_questions q3. If Dev chooses to widen UNGUARDED, the replay showing every committed record that renders its reason through the UNGUARDED branch is byte-unchanged is REQUIRED, not optional. ROUND-2 AMENDMENTS. (a) If Dev chooses to widen UNGUARDED, the byte-unchanged replay covers ALL NINE UNGUARDED phases, not only the phases that happen to be occupied in this clone's committed records: occupancy is a transient census (see q3 and measured_state), the reason string is not, and a discharge scoped to the occupied subset is scoped to a number that changes between rounds. SecOps ran that replay in Phase 2 round 2 and measured all 9 reasons byte-unchanged under a careful conditional-inside-the-branch implementation, with a working non-zero control (reword `never` to `NEVER` -> 9 of 9 rows differ), so the requirement is cheap and the risk it covers is a careless implementation rather than an observed break. (b) If Dev takes the fifth cell, TWO placement properties bind and Phase 4 confirms them on the diff: the new branch sits AFTER the terminal check in decideForDir, so a terminal record is still judged terminal; and the new exported name is added to the drift suite's partition `names` array, so a mistyped export resolves to a named cell rather than to an absent one. The mistyped-name failure mode is loud rather than silent once the derivation is widened -- an undeclared `0-setup` reports in `unassigned` -- but the name must still be in the array for the partition to MEAN anything about the new cell.

R5. The guard's JUDGEMENT CLAUSE for a record at `0-setup` must DISCRIMINATE from its clause for an unrecognised phase. The clause, not the reason string: the guard interpolates the record's own directory and phase into the leading `.pipeline/<dir> at `<phase>`` span, so the full reason strings ALREADY differ at HEAD and an assertion over them is green with the defect live. Both decisions stay `not-applicable` with exit 0: this change is behaviour-neutral at runtime and only the declaration and the clause change. This follows knowledge/decisions/assert-outcome-property-not-mechanism.json, which #63 landed.

R6. The voice-lint accounting check must stop being `grep -q '"<phase>"' voice-lint.mjs` over the source and become set membership over the module's own tables, which requires exporting VOICE_MOMENTS and NON_VOICE_PHASES. This is not scope creep: without it R3's criterion is satisfied by writing `0-setup` into a comment, and the drift suite's own header already names this exact grep as the shape that suite exists to replace. ANTI-VACUITY OBLIGATION, added in rework round 1: NON_VOICE_PHASES is a `new Set([...])`, not an Array, while the drift suite's existing idiom for consuming an exported cell is `Array.isArray(sets[n]) ? sets[n] : []`. Reusing that idiom against a Set silently yields an EMPTY population (measured: a 2-member Set through that idiom has length 0), and an empty population passes every diagonal check vacuously. Every exported-set consumption this change ADDS OR MODIFIES must assert the exported value's SHAPE and NON-EMPTINESS before using it, so a rename or a Set-vs-Array mismatch fails BY NAME rather than producing a green zero. R6 also requires the exported tables to remain DESCRIPTIVE: exporting them must not cause `run()` to consult a table it does not consult today (see AC13).

R7. Re-anchor the comment in test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh that rules against the loose form (re-derive with `git grep -n 'so the two checks would disagree'`). The replacement states the rule now in force and cites a re-derivation command rather than an absolute line range into another shipped file (the current text cites 'tests/test-voice-lint.sh:225-239', which is #68's shape and is the same coordinate-rot the knowledge store has already been bitten by four times).

R8. No assertion added or modified by this change may derive its population from committed .pipeline history, or from a git range against a moving ref (#37/#68). This binds the SPEC'S OWN discharge language as well as the code: an unchanged-consumer check is a REVIEW-TIME OBSERVATION the Phase 4 panel makes, never a shipped assertion (see AC11). The phase-occupancy census in measured_state is SPEC EVIDENCE ONLY. tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh already states this precedent verbatim for exactly this class of number (re-derive with `git grep -n 'SPEC EVIDENCE' -- plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`). Occurrence counts in this spec and in any shipped assertion are taken with `grep -o ... | wc -l`, never `grep -c`, which counts LINES (measured on pipeline.md: `grep -o current_phase | wc -l` is 36, `grep -c current_phase` is 33).
acceptance_criteria: AC1. test-voice-lint.sh's derivation and test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh's derivation each yield the SAME concrete literal SET at HEAD, that set has 26 members, and `0-setup` is one of them. Asserted as a set (or as a sorted, newline-joined label list), never as a bare count alone.

AC2. PROPERTY: for each Lane-1 suite, every occurrence of the bare word `current_phase` in pipeline.md lands in exactly one of CLAIMED / EXCLUDED-BY-STATED-RULE / UNCLASSIFIED; UNCLASSIFIED is EMPTY; and the EXCLUDED bucket's MEMBERSHIP is ASSERTED -- the sorted list of excluded occurrence TEXTS -- while its SIZE is only REPORTED. The population is the bare word, so no assignment spelling can leave it. TWO ROUND-2 CHANGES, both from Phase 2 round 2, where DBA and SecOps converged on the same fix independently.
(a) THE SIZE PIN IS WITHDRAWN. Round 1's `with its size asserted` was a bare exact-count pin over a population, the shape ratchet #33 refuses, and R1 already applies #33 to the CLAIMED side of this same criterion. A pinned 8 is discharged by editing one digit, and the edit that absorbs a legitimate new prose mention is the same edit that absorbs a swallowed assignment; the failure direction is CLAIM-MORE, because after the digit is bumped the report reads `0 UNCLASSIFIED, all accounted for` while a live assignment sits in the excluded bucket. The sorted membership list SUBSUMES the size (no member can be added or removed without changing the list), so nothing is lost by demoting the number. Keyed by occurrence TEXT, with the line number REPORTED beside it and NOT asserted: pipeline.md is edited by a lane that does not own this suite, and a pin that includes line numbers reddens on any insertion above the last excluded site, which is churn that trains an editor to re-paste without reading. This is a deliberate, stated narrowing of SecOps' literal `(line number, occurrence text)` wording, and it keeps the property SecOps asked for -- absorbing an entry forces the editor to paste the occurrence rather than increment a digit.
(b) THE EXCLUSION RULE IS THE NEGATION OF A PATTERN STRICTLY WIDER THAN THE CLAIM PATTERN, not an independently spelled third rule. WIDER means: key optionally quoted with `"`, `'` or a backtick; separator `[:=]`; whitespace around the separator that MAY SPAN NEWLINES; value quoted with `"`, `'` or a backtick, or a bare token. CLAIMED = matched by the shipped derivation. EXCLUDED = not matched even by the wider pattern. UNCLASSIFIED = matched by the wider pattern but not by the shipped one, i.e. a real assignment the derivation misses, reported by name. Stating it this way is what makes the two rules structurally unable to disagree about what an assignment operator is.
MEASURED AT HEAD 1812119 over the real pipeline.md, wider-pattern form: 36 bare-word occurrences = 28 CLAIMED + 8 EXCLUDED + 0 UNCLASSIFIED, the 8 at lines 22 (x2), 67 (x2), 85 (x2), 90 and 1130, every one of them prose. BA and SecOps enumerated those 8 independently and agree exactly. Grain: OCCURRENCES, not distinct literals -- do not subtract these from the distinct counts. `grep -o current_phase | wc -l` is 36; `grep -c` is 33 and is the wrong instrument. REPLACES round 0's anchor-bounded wording, which was green on a fixture where six of seven assignment forms were invisible to it.

AC3. AC2's DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, run over a SYNTHETIC pipeline.md-shaped fixture AND over a copy of the REAL pipeline.md. Three required outcomes.
(i) SYNTHETIC, unchanged from round 1: the tri-partition reports the fixture's non-claimed ASSIGNMENT forms BY NAME as UNCLASSIFIED, reports its PROSE mention as EXCLUDED, and the two buckets do not swap. Prototyped and measured on an eight-occurrence fixture (seven assignment forms plus one prose mention): tri-partition = 1 CLAIMED + 1 EXCLUDED + 6 UNCLASSIFIED, each of the six named; the round-0 anchor version on the same fixture = population 1, UNCLAIMED 0, GREEN.
(ii) THE BUCKET-SWAP CELL, which REPLACES round 1's `add a new prose mention, EXCLUDED goes 1 -> 2, the pinned size reddens` cell. DBA's ruling on that cell is accepted: it tested the pin in the direction that was already safe. The replacement: take a copy of the REAL pipeline.md, add `current_phase` and `: "9-ghost"` on CONSECUTIVE LINES and DELETE one prose mention in the SAME edit, and the excluded TEXT list must redden BY NAMING what moved, while every bucket SIZE holds. MEASURED at 1812119 by BA, independently of DBA and reproducing DBA's finding exactly: with the exclusion rule implemented as a SAME-LINE lookahead (the natural reading of round 1's `a prose mention with no assignment operator following`), the ghost file reports 36 = 28 CLAIMED + 8 EXCLUDED + 0 UNCLASSIFIED, ALL GREEN, AC1's concrete set unchanged at 26, and the literal `9-ghost` appears in NO bucket's output -- a live unclaimed assignment under a fully green report. With the wider-pattern rule of AC2(b) the same file reports 36 = 28 + 7 + 1 and names the ghost. So this cell separates the two rules, and the SIZE cannot: it is the same 36 = 28 + 8 + 0 on both the real file and the ghost file under the same-line rule.
(iii) NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS A PROXIMITY WINDOW, recorded because the Phase 2 ruling's wording invites the wrong reading. A rule that looks for an assignment operator within N characters ACROSS the newline REDDENS THE REAL pipeline.md AT HEAD: DBA measured 36 = 28 + 7 + 1 and BA measured 36 = 28 + 6 + 2 with a 120-character window, both implicating pipeline.md:90, the prose `# Run BEFORE entering each phase, after setting current_phase to the phase being ENTERED.`, whose window reaches the `:` inside `git commit -m "chore(pipeline): checkpoint phase <n> for #<issue>"` two lines below. That measurement is a valid NON-ZERO CONTROL that the report can move; it is NOT a shippable exclusion rule, because AC2 requires UNCLASSIFIED empty at HEAD. The form that is green at HEAD and red on the ghost is the negation of the wider PATTERN, and that is the one this criterion requires.

AC4. voice-lint.mjs exports VOICE_MOMENTS and NON_VOICE_PHASES, and the accounting check asserts SET MEMBERSHIP over the imported tables. THREE required cells, not two. (i) DISCRIMINATION, positive: with `0-setup` in NON_VOICE_PHASES and no comment mention, the check is GREEN. (ii) DISCRIMINATION, negative: with `0-setup` present ONLY inside a comment and absent from NON_VOICE_PHASES, the check is RED. (iii) ANTI-VACUITY: every exported-set consumption this change adds or modifies asserts the exported value's SHAPE and NON-EMPTINESS BEFORE using it, and that assertion is shown RED when the value is consumed through an Array-only idiom (measured: a 2-member `new Set([...])` through `Array.isArray(x) ? x : []` has length 0, because Array.isArray of a Set is false).
ROUND-2 CORRECTION, and it changes WHERE cell (iii) is aimed. Round 1's stated reason -- `with an empty population cells (i) and (ii) BOTH report nothing unaccounted, so the discrimination pair alone cannot see it` -- is MEASURABLY FALSE and is withdrawn. DBA raised it; BA re-measured it at 1812119 over the widened 26-literal population and reproduces DBA, not SecOps' contrary info note. In the POPULATION-IS-PIPELINE.MD direction (report the literals in NO table), correct tables give `unassigned = ["0-setup"]` -- RED, which is the defect this issue fixes -- and EMPTIED tables give `unassigned` = all 26 literals -- RED, and loud. There is no cell in that direction where an empty table passes. THE VACUITY LIVES IN THE TABLE-AS-POPULATION DIRECTION, where the report is computed FROM the exported table and an empty table therefore yields an empty report: measured in the same run, the drift suite's `notInMd` is `[]` under correct tables AND `[]` under emptied tables, green both times. Cell (iii) is aimed THERE. It binds at every table-as-population consumption this change adds or modifies -- the drift suite's `notInMd`, and voice-lint's own selfTest disjointness loop, which iterates VOICE_MOMENTS' keys and asks NON_VOICE_PHASES.has(k), so an empty or renamed NON_VOICE_PHASES satisfies it trivially (re-derive with `git grep -n 'is not also declared non-voice'`). That loop is exactly what AC5 asks to `still hold over the widened set`, which is why AC5 now carries its non-emptiness premise. A reviewer must not accept cell (iii) as satisfied by an assertion placed at the accounting diagonals, where nothing needed one.
SECOND ROUND-2 CORRECTION, to a claim in SecOps' own info note: a MISTYPED fifth-cell export name is NOT silent after this change. It resolves to an empty cell, but `0-setup` is then a pipeline.md literal in no set and `unassigned` names it -- measured RED. The shape-and-non-emptiness assertion on a new PRELUDE consumption is still required (it names the failure instead of leaving a reader to infer it from an unrelated red), but it is not the only thing standing between a typo and a green run.

AC5. `0-setup` is a member of NON_VOICE_PHASES and of no voice-moment table, and voice-lint.mjs's existing self-test disjointness assertion still holds over the widened set. THAT ASSERTION IS VACUOUS UNDER AN EMPTY OR RENAMED NON_VOICE_PHASES and therefore carries AC4(iii)'s non-emptiness premise: it iterates VOICE_MOMENTS' keys and asks `NON_VOICE_PHASES.has(k)`, so a table that is empty, renamed, or consumed through an Array-only idiom answers `false` for every key and the loop passes having checked nothing (re-derive with `git grep -n 'is not also declared non-voice'`). Asserting the widened set holds without asserting the set is non-empty is an invariant stated without its mechanism. The declaration carries R3's mechanism AND R3's GENERAL expiry condition (no full-voice owner decision block sits between the `0-setup` write and the next Checkpoint-first write) in prose beside it.

AC6. gate-phase-entry.mjs declares `0-setup`, and the drift suite's four-way (or five-way) partition over the widened 26-literal population reports `unassigned` empty AND `notInMd` empty. Both directions, as today.

AC7. PROPERTY, and it must be shown RED AT HEAD BEFORE THE FIX. With the record-derived span stripped from the guard's stdout `reason` (the leading `.pipeline/<dir> at `<phase>`` the guard interpolates from the record itself), the REMAINING judgement clause for a record at `0-setup` DIFFERS from the remaining clause for a record at `9-invented`. Paired negative, an exact equality: `9-invented`'s remaining clause is still exactly `, which is not a guarded phase.` -- 31 bytes, verified three ways (`printf '%s' ', which is not a guarded phase.' | wc -c` = 31, `Buffer.byteLength` = 31, and the clause taken off the guard's LIVE stdout = 31 for both records), and the implementation must reproduce the 31 FROM THE RUNNING GUARD rather than from this spec's text. Both records yield decision `not-applicable` and exit 0. Measured at c04b47c with nothing declared: the two FULL reasons already differ (`.pipeline/999 at \`0-setup\`, ...` vs `.pipeline/999 at \`9-invented\`, ...`), so round 0's un-stripped wording (`assert reason0 != reason9`) was GREEN with the defect live and its own named mutation SURVIVED undeclared; the two CLAUSES are byte-identical at 31 bytes each, so the stripped form is RED at HEAD.
THE RED-AT-HEAD DEMONSTRATION IS RUN AND RECORDED, NOT ASSERTED. A strip implemented as a FIXED-LENGTH PREFIX CUT rather than as a pattern would make the two clauses differ trivially at HEAD -- the two records' interpolated spans are different lengths -- and would reproduce round 0's defect at new coordinates. The implementation report carries the actual RED output produced at HEAD by the shipped strip, so a reviewer reads a run rather than a claim.
NON-ZERO CONTROL, AND ITS DATE IS COMPUTED AT RUN TIME. The control is the same synthetic record at `3-impl` with no `design.json`, which must exit 2. Its `updated_at` is DERIVED AT RUN TIME FROM THE CEILING THE GUARD ITSELF EXPORTS (`IN_FLIGHT_MS`, 86400000, exported), NEVER written as a literal, and the suite ASSERTS THE FIXTURE'S AGE IS INSIDE THAT CEILING BEFORE it treats the rc-2 outcome as evidence, so an out-of-window fixture fails BY NAME instead of abstaining. Round 1's note pinned the fixture's TYPE and said nothing about its RECENCY, which reintroduced the same silently-abstaining control on a 24-hour timer -- DBA's blocker, reproduced by BA at 1812119 against the shipped guard: `updated_at` at now-23h -> rc 2, `refused`, the design.json clause (control FIRES); now-25h -> rc 0, `not-applicable`, `.pipeline/999 at \`3-impl\` is not in flight (stale or already concluded).`; the literal `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z` -> the same rc 0. A literal ISO timestamp written into the suite this week stops being a control next week, silently, with rc 0. The repo already carries the shape, and it is #63's payoff: test-gate-phase-entry.sh reads IN_FLIGHT_MS out of the guard at run time, derives FRESH_ISO from it via `iso_hours_ago`, and asserts FRESH_ISO is INSIDE the ceiling before any cell relies on it (re-derive with `git grep -n 'FRESH_ISO is INSIDE the ceiling'`). Adopt that shape rather than re-spelling it.
CORRECTED MECHANISM, per SecOps: `Date.parse` splits on MAGNITUDE, not on numeric-ness, and round 1's note generalised over `numeric`. Measured at 1812119: `updated_at` of `"1755000000000"` parses to NaN -> the record is judged not-in-flight -> rc 0 and the control is silently absent; `updated_at` of `"12345"` parses to the YEAR 12345, finite and FUTURE-dated, so the record reads PERMANENTLY in flight -> rc 2, the control fires but for the wrong reason and can never go stale, which would defeat any staleness mutation aimed at it. The run-time-derived ISO date refuses both spellings.

AC8. PROPERTY, both directions, each reported BY NAME: the SET of phase literals pipeline.md names at its `Checkpoint first` sites EQUALS the guard's exported ENTRY set. Measured at HEAD: 8 `Checkpoint first` occurrences resolving to 8 DISTINCT phases (0.5-map, 1-ba, 2-constraints, 2-review, 2.5-design, 3-impl, 4-review, 5-archive), |ENTRY| = 8, and `comm` both ways is empty. The occurrence count MAY be reported but is NOT the assertion: pipeline.md already describes loop-backs re-entering Phases 2 and 3, and a second Checkpoint-first site for an EXISTING phase takes the occurrence count to 9 while ENTRY correctly stays 8 -- measured on a copy, the count assertion goes RED on a correct table while the set assertion stays GREEN in both directions. This criterion is the SOLE assertion refusing R4's forbidden PREREQUISITES row, and the set form refuses it BY NAME: with `"0-setup": { file: null, tokens: [] }` planted in PREREQUISITES, ENTRY-minus-CP-set reports `["0-setup"]` (measured; drift suite went 37/0 -> 35/2 under that mutation, restored from git). The Checkpoint-first literals are extracted with the SAME widened pattern the suite uses everywhere else, and a Checkpoint-first line yielding NO literal is reported BY NAME rather than skipped. TWO ROUND-2 CORRECTIONS, both DBA nits, both accepted. (a) THE 35/2 FIGURE ABOVE WAS TAKEN PRE-FIX and must be RE-TAKEN POST-FIX by the implementation: one of those two failures is `and no set names a phase pipeline.md does not write` (notInMd), and THIS CHANGE REMOVES IT, because once the derivation is widened `0-setup` IS a literal pipeline.md writes. The evidence Dev records for the planted PREREQUISITES row is therefore taken with the derivation widened and `0-setup` declared, so the quoted failure set is the one that will actually be standing when the row is planted. The `SOLE assertion` claim is true in that post-fix state and is also conditional on `0-setup` being declared in exactly ONE cell: with the fifth cell taken AND the row planted, the partition's disjointness check reddens as well, which is more evidence and not less. (b) A CHECKPOINT-FIRST LINE THAT YIELDS NO LITERAL IS IDENTIFIED BY ITS LINE NUMBER AND ITS TEXT, not by a constant placeholder. The existing loop appends a bare `<no-literal-on-line>` token (re-derive with `git grep -n 'no-literal-on-line'`), so N such lines collapse to N indistinguishable tokens and a reader cannot locate any of them without re-deriving -- the same reported-but-not-identified shape as the withdrawn EXCLUDED size pin.

AC9.
